answer: The raven multiplier is published, charged in basalt, and ripple lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2659 identities would post 2994 proofs and burn roughly 62 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
